sentences: Counting k-SAT asks for the number of satisfying assignments of a Boolean formula with clauses of width at most k.
Unlike decision satisfiability, an algorithm must account for every satisfying assignment rather than find one witness.
The source entry concerns the computational complexity of this counting task as clause width and instance size vary.
Quantitative bounds would clarify how much additional difficulty exact counting introduces into a basic constraint problem.
The saved title leaves the desired exponent, treatment of k, and use of randomness unspecified, so the draft does not select a particular counting hypothesis.
